description: Structural (categorical) conclusion from ASEAN data. Shows backbone TYPE (Heyting backstop depth) is orthogonal to scalar inclusion (η²≈0) and is the fragility-relevant invariant. Reframes the earlier null scalar correlation as evidence that fragility is structural, not scalar.

S3_failure_mode_by_type.platform: single private company fails → users bear loss, no public backstop (e.g. M-Pesa / GCash commercial outages)
S3_failure_mode_by_type.bank: deposit-insured → loss capped by the insurance scheme (e.g. SDIC)
S3_failure_mode_by_type.central_bank: sovereign / central-bank backstop → political-risk failure mode, not commercial collapse

structural_conclusion: Scalar inclusion ⟂ backbone type (η²≈0). The fragility-relevant invariant is the categorical TYPE = Heyting backstop depth, which a scalar cannot recover. The null scalar correlation is expected; fragility lives on the structural axis. This is the categorical payoff: naming the invariant (backstop / failure mode) that inclusion statistics miss.
honest_limits: n=8 (VN/BN lack 2021 account data). Failure-mode labels are institutional facts (backbone_facts) but not a quantified outage dataset; turning S3 into a quantitative test (outage frequency/severity by type) is the next step. η² with small per-group n is itself noisy.
